steps.en: What you see: A continuous jet flows from the descending aorta into the pulmonary trunk through the whole cardiac cycle. The left atrium and left ventricle dilate in significant shunts. The descending aorta shows diastolic flow reversal when the duct is large. Long standing shunts raise pulmonary pressure with right heart enlargement.

Normal values with units: Ductal flow pattern. Normally no continuous flow between aorta and pulmonary trunk. Any continuous jet marks a patent duct.. Source: ASE 2019 transthoracic examination guideline, section on suprasternal views

Left heart volume overload. Diastolic diameter above 58 mm in men or 52 mm in women with a dilated atrium marks a significant shunt.. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left ventricular size

Pulmonary pressure estimate. Tricuspid velocity above 2.8 m per s suggests raised pressure and needs a full right heart study.. Source: ASE 2019 transthoracic examination guideline, section on Doppler and haemodynamics

ECG and heart sound correlation ecg: Left ventricular hypertrophy with a volume pattern marks chronic shunting. Left atrial enlargement follows in large ducts. Right ventricular hypertrophy warns that pulmonary pressure has risen.

ECG and heart sound correlation sounds: A continuous machinery murmur at the left infraclavicular area is classic. Bounding pulses with a wide pulse pressure mark large ducts. A third sound marks left heart volume overload.

What to report: Ductal jet presence with peak systolic and end diastolic velocities
Left heart chamber sizes with the volume overload verdict
Descending aorta reversal and pulmonary pressure estimate
Window quality, probe used and any limitation from air or ribs
Red flags needing urgent referral: Duct dependent circulation in a neonate, needs urgent prostaglandin and paediatric cardiology review
Pulmonary hypertension with right to left ductal flow, needs urgent review before closure is ever discussed
Heart failure in a preterm infant with a large duct, needs urgent neonatal review
Pitfalls: Premature infants keep ducts open for days, so date the study against gestation and postnatal age.
A closed duct leaves a ligament that mimics a wall, so require colour flow before reporting patency.
Endarteritis seeds the pulmonary end of the duct, so look for vegetations in any febrile patient.

todo.en: How to get it on the probe, step by step: Place the patient supine with the neck extended and the probe in the suprasternal notch.
Find the arch in long axis, then rotate slightly to bring the ductal cut into view.
Lower the colour scale to catch low velocity continuous flow at the pulmonary end.
Record continuous wave Doppler through the jet across systole and diastole.
Optimise gain and focus at duct depth, then sweep to short axis to confirm the pulmonary entry.

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Accepting a noisy suprasternal window and missing a small silent duct. Fix: Extend the neck with a shoulder roll and use a small footprint probe with warm gel. Rib shadow and air hide the duct.
Scanning with the focus at the near field and a wide sector. Fix: Place focus exactly at duct depth and narrow the sector. A wide sector at shallow focus blurs the jet.
Relying on one window and skipping the high parasternal sweep. Fix: Sweep the whole trunk from valve to bifurcation. A high parasternal cut catches ducts the suprasternal view misses.

remember.en: State window limitations honestly and pick the confirmatory view.

why.en: Aortic pressure exceeds pulmonary pressure through the whole cycle, so flow never stops.

q.en: The suprasternal window is noisy and the duct is suspected. What first?

o.en: Raise the colour scale to maximum
Extend the neck, focus at duct depth and lower the colour scale

why.en: Position, focus depth and a low colour scale make a small continuous jet visible.

q.en: A cyanotic neonate depends on the duct for pulmonary flow. What next?

o.en: Reassure that all ducts close alone
Urgent prostaglandin and paediatric cardiology review

why.en: Duct dependent circulation collapses if the duct closes, so prostaglandin keeps it open until surgery.

q.en: Which echo pair marks a large significant duct?

o.en: Descending aorta diastolic reversal with dilated left heart

why.en: Runoff into the pulmonary circuit reverses descending aorta flow in diastole while the left heart dilates from the shunt.
